html:
The room in Blender

room.blend (Git LFS) is the source of the 3D room on /. Four scripts rebuild, bake and export it. They run headless with Blender 5.2 LTS, Cycles on the CPU.

build_room.py ──► room.blend ──► bake.py ──► .cache/bake/*.png|exr ──► export.py ──► public/room/
 Henry's layout     (scene)       room atlases (env 4096,               (display-ready)   room.glb (KTX2 + meshopt)
 + room, lights                   desk and props 6144) without the                       window_{sf,delhi}_{day,night}.ktx2
 + room_dressing.py               view; the view's halves alone,                         pale-blue-dot.ktx2, floorplan.json
 + room_art.mjs                   by day and by night                                    poster.avif, poster.jpg
 + window_view.py                                                                        renders/room_v3_*.png, window_view.png

The room (v3, round seven)

                          back wall
   ┌──────────────────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────────────┐
   │ posters + plaque      │ desk, monitor,   │ window 1.5 x 1.44 m  │  right return wall
   │ credenza, lava lamp   │ shelf, pennant   │ mango on the sill    │  (ends at y = -2.0)
 d ├┐                                                               │ bookcase, Voyager,
 o ││ hallway                                                       │ Pale Blue Dot,
 o ├┘                                                               │ Japanese-lit print
 r │ Instax board                                       │ projector high on its
   │ roller screen ◄───────────────────────────────────── wall shelf (y = -2.0)
   │ mini kitchen: counter, espresso,          armchair   record cabinet + turntable,
   │ oven, rolls, bagels, pour-over,                      crate, paper lantern
   │ shelf, pendant
   └── open front ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

The floor is 6.4 x 4.4 m and the walls 2.85 m. A ceiling band, the ceiling cut 0.42 m from the walls with a cornice, runs along all three walls, so from the wide framing the room has a ceiling edge instead of bare wall tops; the right return wall ends in a painted wall end, and a doorway near the back of the left wall opens onto a dim hallway lit by a sconce.

Re-bake

blender -b blender/room.blend -P blender/scripts/bake.py

room.blend reads its downloaded textures, models and font from blender/.cache/ (git-ignored), so on a fresh clone run the rebuild below once before baking. Bakes the three room atlases (env 4096², desk and props 6144²) at 160 samples with OIDN denoising, then each half of the window view (window_sf, window_delhi; 1280² each) by day and by night, on 16 threads (the devbox is shared), and saves the bake UVs into room.blend. The desk and props atlases bake larger than they ship (export.py resamples them), so each shipped texel averages several baked ones. The room atlases bake without the view (a camera-invisible card behind the window, lit by Poly Haven's dusk HDRI, lights the room); the view bakes alone with its own sun, sky and night lights. For a quick look, bake small: -- --scale 0.25 --samples 32, one atlas: -- --atlas desk, or the view only: -- --atlas window_sf,window_delhi. The final bake took 71 minutes on 24 threads of the shared devbox (env 9, desk 30, props 31, the view 1.5).

Re-export

blender -b blender/room.blend -P blender/scripts/export.py

Renders the stills, writes the view's four KTX2 files (ETC1S with mipmaps, ktx create) and pale-blue-dot.ktx2 (NASA/JPL's PIA23645, cropped square, 1024 px), exports the glb, then runs gltf-transform 4.5.1 (via npx): dedup, prune (empties and attributes kept), KTX2 ETC1S atlases, meshopt geometry. The atlases ship resampled from their bakes (EXPORT_SIZES: env 2560, desk 3584, props 3072; the view's halves ship at their 1280 px bake). It then points each view half's material at its day texture by URI and writes public/room/floorplan.json (floorplan.py). It fails if room.glb is over 4.9 MB, the two day textures are over 560 KB together, a node from the contract below is missing, or a removed one is back. Needs Node (npx), ktx from KTX-Software 4.x and ffmpeg with libaom on PATH. -- --no-stills exports only the glb and textures; -- --only room_v3_idle,window_view renders some stills.

Stills: renders/room_v3_{idle,desk,window,kitchen,oven,shelf,space,armchair,projector,photos,posters,records,lava}.png beside the round-two renders/room_*.png, renders/window_view.png (the cam_window framing, plain) and public/room/poster.{avif,jpg} (the cam_idle view). They show San Francisco at dusk and Delhi by day, the four Letterboxd favourites from public/room/posters/, the photographs the collection marks for the wall (src/content/photography/, onWall, in its order) on the Instax board and the phrases from src/content/sticky-notes.json on the sticky notes; the roller screen is rolled up. In the glb those pictures are runtime textures, so re-export the stills when the favourites or the wall's photographs change.

Rebuild from scratch

blender -b --factory-startup -P blender/scripts/build_room.py

Downloads Henry Heffernan's three models (pinned commit, checked by sha256), the CC0 textures, HDRI and models from Poly Haven and ambientCG, Newsreader (pinned commit, sha256) and NASA's Pale Blue Dot Revisited (sha256) into blender/.cache/, runs room_art.mjs (Node) for the typographic art, then builds the scene and overwrites room.blend. Props are appended from blender/props/<name>.blend (root collection named after the prop; rebuild them with python3 blender/scripts/props_build.py --render). Re-bake after a rebuild. ROOM_QUICK=1 skips the window view for layout work, and ROOM_BLEND=<path> writes the scene elsewhere.

window_view.py also renders the view alone for quick work on it: blender -b --factory-startup -P blender/scripts/window_view.py -- <out_dir> day cam_window. preview.py renders quick looks of room.blend from named or ad-hoc framings, texel_density.py reports the shipped texels per metre per atlas, and node blender/scripts/glb_stats.mjs prints the glb's bytes, draw calls, triangles and textures.

What the glb holds

Node What
zone_* empties at the origin (identity) that group the meshes by part of the room: zone_desk, zone_window, zone_posters, zone_wall_space (bookcase and space wall), zone_photos, zone_projector, zone_records, zone_reading, zone_kitchen, zone_room (the shell); cameras, markers and click boxes stay at the root
env_* walls (env_wall_back, env_wall_left, env_wall_right), floor, ceiling band and cornice, doorway, door, hallway, window, curtains, sill, radiator, desk shelf, fixtures, rugs, the projector's shelf, the record cabinet, credenza, kitchen tiles, top and shelf, photo lamp
desk_* desk, chair, computer, CRT, keyboard, mouse, cables, lamp, papers, mug, notebook, headphones; photo_album
props_* props from blender/props/ and the dressing (books, records, plants, frames, lantern, jacket, jars …)
crt_glow, lamp_bulb, lava_lamp_glass, oven_glow, nas_led_0..3 runtime meshes, each with its own unlit material (nas_led is shared by the four LEDs) so the site can tint, flicker or replace them
window_view_sf, window_view_delhi the view's halves (the seam runs behind the window's central mullion, x = 1.85 m); material = that half's day texture by URI; extras texture_day, texture_night
poster_art_0..3, poster_plaque the poster pictures on the back wall, slot 0 leftmost seen from the room (art scheme below); the plaque "Four favourites — from Letterboxd", engraved and baked
photo_board, instax_slot_0..19 the Instax board on the left wall (cork, oak frame, pins, tape, string, baked) and its twenty prints, each a quad with the art scheme over the whole card; extras instax_slot, format (mini or wide), width_m, height_m, aspect, angle_deg, image_uv (the picture's area on the card: x0, y0, x1, y1)
roller_screen_housing, roller_screen, projection_surface the pull-down screen on the left wall: the case (baked), the screen modelled fully down (extras drop_m, width_m; the site scales it from its top edge) and the 16:9 picture on its face, 0.90 x 0.506 m, art scheme (the film plays on it), extras width_m, height_m, aspect; both baked rolled up (the wall behind lit, the projector's lamp off)
print_pale_blue_dot the square Pale Blue Dot print, art scheme; extras texture = pale-blue-dot.ktx2
sticky_note_0..5 paper notes, art scheme (the site writes the phrase); 0–2 on the monitor bezel, 3–5 on the wall right of the monitor; extras paper (hex), where
kitchen_counter, espresso_machine, espresso_cup, espresso_coffee the kitchen nook's counter and the machine; the cup (with its saucer) and the coffee's surface are their own nodes: the surface sits at the full level, extras fill_depth_m 0.026 (lower it that far, raise it while pouring)
countertop_oven, oven_door, croissant the oven body; oven_door is a pivot on the bottom hinge axis holding oven_door_mesh (extras turn_axis +X, open_angle_deg 82: turn about local +X, the top swings toward the room); the croissant on the rack inside
lava_lamp the lamp's baked body, alone on the credenza under the posters
projector, projector_reel_front, projector_reel_rear, projector_dial the projector on its wall shelf at the right return wall's front end, facing the roller screen across the room; the reels and the program dial are pivots (empties on their axles) holding <name>_mesh, extras turn_axis (glTF axes); the dial's program_angles_deg as before
record_player, platter, tonearm, record_crate, record_sleeve_0..5 the turntable on the record cabinet (baked); platter is a pivot at the spindle (extras turn_axis +Y, rpm 33.333) holding the platter, mat and record; tonearm is a pivot at the arm's base (extras turn_axis +Y and, in degrees counterclockwise seen from above, rest_angle_deg 0, play_angle_deg at the outer groove, end_angle_deg at the inner groove); the crate of six LPs, whose sleeve fronts are quads with the art scheme, extras sleeve_slot, width_m, height_m, aspect
bookshelf, book_spine_<slug> the bookcase on the right return wall, and the six books standing together on its middle shelf (typographic spines and covers baked), extras title, author, year; slugs the-wind-up-bird-chronicle, kafka-on-the-shore, 1q84, kitchen, on-earth-were-briefly-gorgeous, the-elegant-universe
print_japanese_lit, pennant_gatech, voyager_record the Japanese-literature print leaning on the bookcase, the Georgia Tech pennant over the desk shelf, the Voyager record in its shadow box on the space wall (all baked)
mango_fruit the mango on the plant on the window sill
hit_* invisible click boxes (material proxy): hit_mango, hit_nas, hit_window, hit_fujifilm_a (the camera on the desk; the shelf cameras have none), hit_projector, hit_projector_dial, hit_lava_lamp, hit_espresso, hit_oven, hit_croissant, hit_books, hit_voyager, hit_pale_blue_dot, hit_print_japanese_lit, hit_pennant_gatech, hit_photo_board, hit_record_player, hit_album, hit_plaque; hit_poster_<id> keep their T3 names and carry extras poster_slot
monitor_screen centre of the CRT glass; local +Z out of the glass; extras width_m, height_m
projector_lens, projector_screen_center beam origin (local −Z along the beam) and the centre of the picture on the roller screen when it is down
lava_lamp_light, espresso_spout, espresso_steam the lamp's light centre; where the coffee stream starts (it falls straight down); where steam rises over the cup
album_open_anchor where the opened album floats, 0.55 m in front of cam_desk, local +Z toward the camera; extras width_m, height_m
cam_* + cam_*_target camera framings with look-at empties, extras fov_deg (35, vertical): cam_loading, cam_idle (the wide view), cam_desk (the landing frame, monitor readable), cam_monitor, cam_arrival_0..2 (the arrival glide: past the window, past the mango plant, onto the desk), cam_tour_0..10 (the tour's stops, below), cam_window, cam_shelf (the books), cam_photos (the whole board), cam_projector (the screen, the projector behind the camera), cam_record_player, cam_espresso, cam_oven

The tour's stops, in order (also in floorplan.json): 0 desk, 1 window, 2 bookshelf, 3 space wall, then 4 kitchen nook, 5 lava lamp, 6 projector, 7 photo board, 8 posters, 9 armchair corner, 10 record player.

Units are metres, +Y up. Every material is KHR_materials_unlit with the baked light as its base colour, already tone-mapped (AgX, exposure 2.45, the same as the stills), so the site shows it with no tone mapping and sRGB output. The atlas materials are room_env, room_desk and room_props; only room_props_leaves (the mango leaves, same texture as room_props) is double-sided, because thin closed shells z-fight through a double-sided material.

The art scheme: the light on the picture is baked on white paper, so the site can draw art × light: put the runtime art in map (TEXCOORD_0, 0–1 over the picture), move the baked texture to lightMap (GLTFLoader already gives it channel 1) and set lightMapIntensity to π. For the view, blend window_<half>_day.ktx2 and window_<half>_night.ktx2 by that city's local time; to soften the seam, blend by world x across the seam instead of per mesh (both halves' textures match at the seam in each state).

public/room/floorplan.json is the room's plan for the tour map, in glTF world X and Z (metres): outline (the floor), walls, doors, windows (segments), furniture (labelled footprints) and stops (id, label, camera node, position), written from the blend by floorplan.py.

Lights

Each light has a source in the room: the desk lamp (tungsten, about 2700 K), dusk through the window (an emissive card behind the window and a soft area light), the brass picture light over the posters, the lava lamp's glow on them, the strip light under the desk shelf, the Instax board's picture lamp, the kitchen pendant over the counter and the light bar under the kitchen shelf, the oven's elements, the CRT glass, the paper lantern beside the record cabinet (kept below the desk lamp and the CRT), and a sconce in the hallway beyond the door. There is no ceiling light. The projector's lamp is off in the bake: the screen rests rolled up, and the site lights the beam while the film runs. A camera-invisible ceiling, front wall and the open stretch of the right side bounce light like a closed room; they are never baked or exported. The view has its own lights (sun and sky by day; moon, floodlights on the monuments and the bridge, city glow by night) in window_lights, switched on only while its halves bake.

Budget

The glb holds about 122k triangles in 145 draw calls (round two: 112k in 108); the renderer culls per object, so a close framing submits 13 to 68 calls. Shipped density: desk 798 texels per metre, props 284, env 118 (the room's surfaces grew from 66 to 175 m² inside the same byte budget). -- --merge-static joins the plain scenery per atlas (fewer calls, coarser culling); it is off. The props' prop files keep their full detail, and build_room.py decimates the densest ones for the room only (DECIMATE). The view keeps only faces some framing, or a glide the site makes, can see through the window. Credits for every downloaded model, texture, HDRI and font are in ASSETS.md.
